newsitem.title: CANADA: Second Cup sees better performance.
newsitem.headline: Second Cup sees better performance.

text.p: Gourmet coffee retailer The Second Cup Ltd said it expects to post better results after reporting a first quarter loss from weak performances by some of its U.S. outlets.

"We expect to report improved performance in upcoming quarters and we remain optimistic," said chief executive officer Michael Bregman. "Our ability to generate strong short-term profitability will depend largely on the pace at which our U.S. improvement programs take effect."
The coffee house chain lost C$0.04 a share in the first quarter ended September 21 after a year-earlier gain of C$0.03.
Second Cup said recently it was interested in selling its poorly performing U.S. stores outside of Arizona.

President of Canadian operations Lucio Di Clemente said that the retailer will open more stores in Canada this fiscal year. "The pace of our expansion in Canada is accelerating and we expect a record year of growth."
Second Cup also recently invested C$6.5 million in The Great Canadian Bagel Ltd, the nation's largest operator of bagel making shops.
The two companies have said they will accelerate a program that involves two services operating out of one location, commonly called twinning. So far there are three such locations in Canada.
